newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ share prices end static, Power NZ dampens index.
newsitem.headline: NZ share prices end static, Power NZ dampens index.

text.p: * New Zealand share prices end flat on light turnover
* Power NZ slide dampens top 40 index
* Enerco down on profit downgrades
Price movements at close
LAST CHG * NZSE40 cap index +0.81 at 2,296.20
134 nil * NZSE-10 cap index +2.96 at 1,150.00
328 +1 * NZSC cap index -1.50 at 5,009.38
315 -1 * NZMC .NZMC cap index -4.69 at 1,854.31

671 +1 * Other movers - -40 -30
New Zealand share prices ended Wednesday's trade with a flat tone, the market finding short rates of over 7.00 percent a major hurdle.
Also putting a dampener on the NZSE-40 Capital Index was a 40-cent decline in constituent stocks Power NZ and Enerco.
The index ended just 0.81 of a point up at 2,296.20 on turnover worth NZ$44 million.
Murray Rutherford at SBC Warburg said it was a disappointing response to Wall Street's 75-point gain.
Telecom, four days into phase two of its share buyback, accounted for about NZ$14 million of the day's volume.
Power NZ dropped 40 cents to NZ$6.10, now that a prolonged battle for control between Utilicorp and Mercury appears to be over.
Utilicorp and Mercury, now linked as joint venture partners, are to offer minority Power NZ shareholders NZ$6.00 a share.

"No one knows what's going to happen there other than the likelihood of further rationalisation has drawn closer now that the issue of effective control of Power NZ has been solved by way of the joint venture," Rutherford said.
Enerco's ENZ.NZ 30-cent slide to NZ$5.35 came on the back of broker profit downgrades since its result last Friday.
The downgrades were a reflection on the slowdown in the economy and Enerco's exposure to the industrial sector.
Elsewhere the market was largely unchanged, exceptions being Lion Nathan, which firmed five to NZ$3.62, and INL up 15 at $7.50.
Fernz Corp, after announcing the sale of its New Zealand fertiliser business, was unchanged at NZ$4.72. Brokers were still assessing the impact of the NZ$105 million divestment.
-- James Gray, Auckland newsroom +64 9 302 1253
